extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411, 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Audio was downloaded using LibriLight tools. Text sources were retrieved from Project Gutenberg and other domains via automated parsers or manual extraction. Pseudo-labels were generated using acoustic models, and transcripts were retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to source text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks and Project Gutenberg text data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz and segmented into 10-20 second segments using acoustic models and silence detection. Text was normalized (NFKC, removal of punctuation/special characters, hyphenation handling). Transcripts were retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to source text using TF-IDF and Smith-Waterman alignment. Candidate transcripts with WER > 40% were filtered. Numbers were replaced with aligned words from pseudo-labels. Hyphens and apostrophes were handled via heuristics.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio segmentation into 10-20s clips. Text normalization including NFKC, character filtering, and hyphen/apostrophe correction. Transcript retrieval via alignment. Filtering of corrupted metadata, multi-speaker audio, and duplicate book versions. Splitting into train/dev/test sets ensuring no speaker overlap and balanced gender/duration. Human verification of dev/test sets to correct obvious errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo-labels were generated using beam-search decoding with acoustic models. Transcripts were retrieved by aligning pseudo-labels with source book text. Human transcribers listened to audio and corrected 'clear and obvious' errors in the development and test sets to ensure high quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human verification was performed on development and test sets. The Word Error Rate (WER) between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts was measured (Table 3) to assess quality. Transcribers were instructed to only correct clear and obvious errors to avoid adding bias.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human transcribers were used for verification of dev/test sets. Gender of speakers was determined using a SVM classifier trained on LibriSpeech data, with manual checks on Dutch and Polish subsets.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere, KenLM, pdftotext, num2words (mentioned as alternative), SVM classifier for gender prediction.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. No specific versioning or update schedule is mentioned, but it is released under a public domain license.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender of speakers (predicted via classifier and manually checked for some languages).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to open new avenues in ASR and TTS research, particularly for multilingual and low-resource languages, by providing a large-scale, openly licensed benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from audiobooks, which may reflect biases in the types of books available on Project Gutenberg and LibriVox. The gender classifier used for splitting data had high accuracy but was not perfect. The dataset focuses on 8 specific languages, potentially underrepresenting others.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to read speech from audiobooks. Text sources were not available for all audiobooks, leading to data loss. The transcript retrieval process is not perfect, as evidenced by WER metrics. The dataset does not include conversational speech. Some languages have significantly less data than English.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research.
